The main takeaway from our work is that

KSHV encodes a protein (KapB, encoded by the Kaposin B gene) that is capable of activating the MK2-hsp-27-p115RHOGEF-Rho-kinase signaling axis, and that this signaling axis is required to cause the post-transcriptionally-mediated effects of KapB.

KSHV infection causes a reprogramming of endothelial cells (EC) to a more secretory phenotype, and that the virus accomplishes this, in part, by activating a stress kinase called MK2, which in turn causes a reorganization of cytoskeletal structures called stress fibers, and also causes the disassembly of structures called processing bodies (PBs).
KapB is a key contributor to KSHV reprogramming of endothelial cells (ECs) and that this protein is capable of eliciting multiple phenotypes that are characteristic of KS tumor ECs.
